title: に (time, destination, location of existence, indirect object)
meaning: "at / on / in / to / for" — a point in time, destination, place where something exists, recipient.
simpleExplanation: に is the "point" particle. It marks a point in time (六時に "at six"), the point where something exists (机の上に "on the desk"), the point you go to (学校に "to school") and the person something goes to (友達に "to a friend"). If you can imagine an arrow landing on a spot, に is usually the right choice.
whenUsed: Clock times, days, dates; where things and people are (あります・います・住んでいます); destinations with 行く・来る・帰る・入る; the person you give to, write to, phone or meet (あげる・書く・電話する・会う).
formation: Time + に  (三時に、日曜日に)
Place + に + あります／います／住んでいます
Place + に + 行きます／来ます／帰ります
Person + に + あげます／書きます／電話します／会います

examples.note: Point in time: 六時に "at six".

examples.en: There is a book on the desk.

examples.reading: ともだちに てがみを かきます。

examples.ja: 友達に電話をかけました。

examples.note: The person you call is marked with に.

similarGrammar.difference: で marks where an ACTION happens (図書館で勉強する); に marks where something IS (図書館にいる).
へ is direction (toward); に is the arrival point. With 行く／来る both are fine.
Clock times and days take に; 今日・明日・毎日 take nothing.

commonMistakes.why: Studying is an action, so the place takes で. に is for where something exists or where you go.
Relative time words (今日, 明日, 来週) never take に.

commonMistakes.wrong: 友達を手紙を書きます。
commonMistakes.right: 友達に手紙を書きます。
commonMistakes.why: The person receiving the letter takes に; only the letter takes を.

usageNotes: Specific times take に (三時に, 月曜日に, 2020年に); relative times do not (今日, 明日, 来週, 毎日 — no に). Frequency: 一週間に二回 "twice a week".
jlptTips: Look at the verb: あります・います・住んでいます・行きます・来ます・帰ります → に. Action verbs like 食べます・勉強します・会議をします → で.
Clock times, days of the week and dates take に. If the options are に and nothing (×) after 明日 or 毎日, choose nothing.
